incident: The mega-container ship Ever Given ran aground on 23 March 2021 and wedged across the Suez Canal for about six days, halting all traffic and stranding hundreds of waiting vessels until tugs refloated it on 29 March.
Houthi attacks in the Red Sea drove most shippers to reroute around the Cape of Good Hope, cutting Suez Canal traffic by roughly half by early 2024 and reducing canal revenues by up to 60 percent.
A severe El Nino drought forced the Panama Canal Authority to cut daily transits to about 32 ships by August 2023, producing a backlog of roughly 115 waiting vessels.
Record-low water in Gatun Lake pushed the canal to reduce daily crossings to 24 from 7 November 2023 with tightened draft limits before rains allowed transit slots to be raised again through 2024.
Houthi forces used a helicopter to board and seize the vehicle carrier Galaxy Leader in the southern Red Sea on 19 November 2023, holding its 25 crew for more than a year.
The fertiliser-laden bulk carrier Rubymar, struck by a Houthi missile on 18 February 2024, sank on 2 March 2024, becoming the first vessel lost in the Red Sea campaign.
A Houthi anti-ship missile struck the bulk carrier True Confidence in the Gulf of Aden on 6 March 2024, killing three seafarers in the first fatal attack of the campaign.

The Greek-flagged crude tanker Sounion, carrying nearly one million barrels of oil, was set ablaze and disabled by projectiles near Hodeidah on 21 August 2024 in an attack attributed to Houthi forces, raising fears of a major spill.
Houthi forces sank the bulk carriers Magic Seas and Eternity C in the Red Sea in early July 2025, killing at least three crew and taking others captive in a sharp re-escalation of attacks.
Russia's February 2022 invasion and naval blockade of Ukraine's Black Sea ports halted maritime grain exports, cutting outbound commercial sailings from more than 150 a day to near zero.
Russia terminated its participation in the Black Sea Grain Initiative on 17 July 2023, ending the protected corridor that had allowed more than 32 million tonnes of Ukrainian grain exports.
Days after quitting the grain deal, Russia launched a second consecutive night of missile and drone strikes on the port city of Odesa on 19 July 2023.
Two oil tankers, the Front Altair and Kokuka Courageous, were attacked and set ablaze in the Gulf of Oman near the Strait of Hormuz on 13 June 2019, forcing the evacuation of 44 crew.
Iran's Revolutionary Guard seized the British-flagged tanker Stena Impero in the Strait of Hormuz on 19 July 2019 and held the ship and its 23 crew for about two months.
Iran's navy seized the Marshall Islands-flagged tanker Advantage Sweet in the Gulf of Oman near the Strait of Hormuz on 27 April 2023 and detained it for more than a year.
Iranian forces boarded and seized the tanker St Nikolas in the Gulf of Oman near the Strait of Hormuz on 11 January 2024 in retaliation for a US oil confiscation.
After US strikes on Iranian nuclear sites, Iran's parliament backed closing the Strait of Hormuz on 22 June 2025, though the measure was not enacted, spiking global oil-market fears.
A Turkish proof-of-insurance requirement introduced in December 2022 stranded a backlog of up to 27 oil tankers in the Turkish Straits amid the G7 Russian-oil price cap.

incident: Drought dropped the Mississippi River to a record low of -10.79 feet at Memphis on 17 October 2022, grounding barges and idling well over 100 towboats during peak grain-shipping season.

Hurricane Ida made landfall in Louisiana as a Category 4 storm on 29 August 2021, closing the Port of New Orleans and shutting Lower Mississippi vessel traffic and Gulf Coast port operations.
